newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian radical communists forge new bloc.
newsitem.headline: Russian radical communists forge new bloc.

text.p: Russian hardline communist groups forged a new alliance on Sunday, the latest move in a re-alignment of leftist forces after the defeat of Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov in July's presidential election.

The new movement, called Communist and Socialist Forces of Russia, unites a number of radical groups but not Zyuganov's mainstream party. Zyuganov was beaten by Boris Yeltsin in July's presidential election run-off.

A declaration and charter adopted at a congress said the new movement wanted to restore the Soviet Union and "workers' power", abolish the presidency and return property to the people, Interfax news agency said.

The new bloc comprises a number of radical groups, including the Russian Communist Workers' Party (RCWP), the Officers' Union and a splinter group of the Working Russia movement, led by Vladimir Grigoryev.
Working Russia, under the leadership of former journalist Viktor Anpilov, just failed to capture the five percent of the vote needed to win seats in December's parliamentary election.
But a fist fight broke out at its congress this month and a splinter group broke away under Grigoryev.
Zyuganov's party emerged as the biggest party in December's poll, controlling a third of the 450-seat lower house.
But the left has been through a period of soul-searching since Zyuganov's defeat in the presidential election.
In August, Zyuganov's party and its allies formed the National Patriotic Union, with the stress on nationalism rather than socialism, to challenge Yeltsin.
